verdict.rationale: Bitwarden has substantial programmatic surfaces. The CLI is billed as "fully-featured" for vault management, and its `bw serve` mode exposes the vault as a local RESTful Vault Management API with an OpenAPI document. A separate Public API covers organization admin (members, collections, groups, event logs, policies) via OAS3/Swagger. However, no evidence documents UI-to-API parity: the vault API needs a locally run CLI server rather than a hosted endpoint, and features such as vault health reports run locally in the client with no API counterpart shown. missing for 10: explicit documented UI/API parity, hosted vault-item REST API (not local-only bw serve), API coverage of reports/import/export and other UI features, independent hands-on corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Bitwarden command-line interface (CLI) is a powerful, fully-featured tool for accessing and managing your vault.
The Bitwarden Public API provides organizations a suite of tools for managing members, collections, groups, event logs, and policies.
the CLI whose documented `bw serve` mode exposes the whole vault as a local RESTful API (Vault Management API)
Using the personal API key for CLI authentication is suitable for automated workflows
